Location: Remote - United States only.

About the role:

Ottimate is building the AI-native future of accounts payable. Our platform processes millions of invoices across hundreds of enterprise customers, powered by a suite of ML models and agentic workflows. As Director of AI Engineering, you will own the full AI and ML layer of our product — from invoice understanding and vendor intelligence to our conversational AP Copilot and the next generation of autonomous AP agents.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will spend at least half your time writing code, architecting systems, and driving technical decisions alongside your team. You will also set the AI roadmap, partner cross-functionally with Product, Data, and Platform Engineering, and manage a distributed team of 8–10 engineers across Data and ML.

We are looking for a senior technical manager or director — ideally someone who has thrived at a smaller company and is ready for a career step up into broader ownership. If you are energized by shipping real AI products, working with noisy real-world financial data, and building the systems that will define how enterprises automate AP, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Technical Leadership

  • Architect and ship production AI/ML systems — you write code, not just review it
  • Own the AI roadmap end-to-end: prioritization, trade-offs, delivery
  • Set technical standards for model quality, evals, observability, and reliability
  • Drive adoption of agentic coding tools to multiply team velocity
  • Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or equivalent — measure and improve PR throughput
  • Partner with Platform Engineering on infrastructure, data pipelines, and APIs

People & Cross-Functional

  • Manage a distributed team of 8–10 engineers across Data and ML disciplines
  • Hire, develop, and retain engineers at all levels; build a high-trust remote culture
  • Partner with Product on roadmap sequencing and scope trade-offs
  • Work directly with customer-facing teams to close feedback loops on model quality
  • Communicate AI capabilities and limitations clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Model & Systems Ownership

  • Own model performance metrics and drive continuous improvement pipelines
  • Build and maintain evals frameworks — regression suites, human review, A/B testing
  • Oversee training data collection, curation, and labeling operations
  • Manage the full ML lifecycle: experimentation, deployment, monitoring, iteration
  • Define and enforce quality bars for agentic workflows entering production

Requirements

Applied AI & Agentic Systems

  • Production agentic pipelines using frontier models
  • Anthropic SDK · OpenAI SDK · tool use, function calling, multi-agent orchestration
  • Reliable agent loop design — planning, memory, tool execution, error recovery
  • RAG pipeline design — chunking, embedding models, retrieval tuning, reranking
  • Evals frameworks built from scratch — correctness, regression, semantic similarity
  • Observability for production AI — tracing, cost tracking, latency, failure analysis

Model Expertise

  • Fine-tuning frontier or open-source models for domain-specific tasks
  • LoRA, QLoRA, instruction tuning — not just off-the-shelf API calls
  • Training data collection, curation, cleaning, and labeling at scale
  • LLM inference and serving optimization
  • vLLM, TGI, or equivalent
  • Model selection trade-offs — cost, latency, capability, context window

Engineering Depth

  • Hands-on Python — comfortable writing, reviewing, and shipping production code
  • PostgreSQL — schema design, query optimization, indexing strategies
  • Distributed systems — async workers, queues, retries, state machines
  • Celery or similar async task frameworks is a bonus
  • Public-facing API design — REST, versioning, developer experience
  • MCP server development — tool-accessible APIs for AI agent integration
  • AWS or cloud infrastructure — enough to own AI workload deployments

Ideal Career Background

  • Engineering Manager ready for director-level ownership
  • Has led technical teams at a startup or growth-stage company — knows how to move fast
  • Hands-on contributor who has also managed small high performance teams.
  • Comfortable owning outcomes

★ Industry Experience

  • Finance and/or AP domain — invoice workflows, GL coding, vendor management
  • Hospitality — high-volume, multi-location AP operations
  • Noisy, unstructured text data — OCR outputs, inconsistent supplier formats, entity resolution at scale

★ Industry experience above is a bonus

Exceptional AI engineering skills are the primary bar. We will teach the domain.

Benefits

We care deeply about making Ottimate an incredible place to work and invest a significant amount of time and energy into creating and maintaining a company culture that provides our team with a generous level of support whilst inspiring them to do their best work.

The specific benefits/perks we offer are continually evolving, but currently include:

  • Compensation: 200,000-225,000 + 15% Annual Bonus + Equity
  • Competitive salary based on skills & experience.
  • Medical, Dental, Vision and other Company-Subsidized Benefits for you and your family.
  • Employer sponsored 401(k) with company match.
  • Paid Time Off (and the encouragement to use it).
  • Annual company retreats.
  • Promote from within philosophy.

Beyond the tangible benefits though:

  • You will be part of a growing team, at a pinnacle moment of scale for the business, and experience the excitement of working in a startup where each action makes a huge difference.
  • You will have the agency to solve difficult problems creatively, the freedom to explore work that inspires you, and infrastructure to ensure you're constantly challenged and developing.

  • Our leaders lead with a people-first approach; inspiring excellence, nurturing ideas, and finding creative ways to eliminate obstacles for cultivating growth.

jobs.title: Product Manager - DBS
jobs.excerpt: Bnberry is transforming the $87 billion travel tech industry by changing how hotels and resorts connect with guests worldwide.
jobs.description:
Bnberry is transforming the $87 billion travel tech industry by changing how hotels and resorts connect with guests worldwide. We’re building DBS — a new kind of product that hotels adopt as a B2B SaaS business tool, and that travelers experience directly as a consumer-facing hotel booking journey.

This is not a Product Owner or delivery-management role focused on writing tickets and managing developers. Your mandate is to own DBS end-to-end, connecting three product areas that most companies keep separate: the guest-facing booking experience, the hotel-facing workflows and business value, and how travelers discover hotels through search and AI tools.

What You’ll Own

  • The consumer-facing booking journey — including the logic behind it: availability, rates, cancellation policies, and how PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations shape what the guest sees
  • Hotel-facing workflows tied to DBS: onboarding, reporting, and adoption
  • The product capabilities that help hotels improve and measure visibility across search engines and AI discovery tools, in partnership with Marketing and relevant specialists
  • Booking-funnel performance and conversion
  • The link between guest experience and measurable hotel business value

What You’ll Do

  • Define product vision and roadmap for DBS, connecting guest booking UX, hotel workflows, and AI discovery into one coherent product
  • Own the booking journey end-to-end — identify friction in calendars, date selection, room/rate selection, checkout, and confirmation, and understand how availability, rates, cancellation policies, and PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations affect what the guest experiences; work with Engineering on dependencies and failure cases
  • Translate hotel onboarding, reporting, and adoption needs into product decisions that show measurable business value to hotel customers
  • Own the product capabilities behind search and AI/GEO visibility — partner with Marketing and relevant specialists on execution, while building enough SEO/GEO literacy to identify and prioritize the right product bets
  • Interview hoteliers and travelers and run usability tests; translate qualitative and quantitative findings into clear priorities
  • Define success metrics before building, and use experiment results to guide iteration
  • Work closely with Design and Engineering through detailed user journeys, making trade-offs and shipping in small, practical iterations
  • Align Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success around DBS priorities, and take responsibility for product outcomes

Requirements

  • 3+ years of product management experience owning customer-facing products, including relevant experience in hospitality technology or travel booking
  • Relevant, demonstrable connection to the US market
  • Hands-on customer research skills — hotelier and traveler interviews, usability testing, and translating findings into clear priorities
  • Strong analytical and experimentation skills — diagnosing booking-funnel friction, testing improvements, and measuring booking conversion, hotel adoption, and retention
  • Comfortable working through detailed user journeys with Design and Engineering, making trade-offs, and shipping in small iterations
  • Able to operate independently with ambiguity, prioritize by customer and business value, and align Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success

    What We’re Looking For:

Industry-Grounded — You’ve worked in hotel technology, B2B hospitality platforms, or a B2C travel product with an actual booking journey. Deep exposure to hotel distribution systems is a plus, not a prerequisite — strong B2C travel/booking experience counts too.

US Market Fluent — You have demonstrable familiarity with US hotels or travel customers, whether through working with them directly or through living and studying in the US combined with hospitality experience.

Booking UX Owner — You understand the details of a booking flow — calendars, date selection, room and rate choice, checkout, confirmation — and the logic behind it: availability, rates, cancellation policies, and PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations. You can spot friction before a customer complains about it.

Fluent in Both Guest and Hotel — You’re as comfortable reasoning about a traveler’s booking journey as you are about a hotelier’s onboarding, adoption, and ROI.

Fast Learner on AI/SEO — You understand how travelers discover hotels through search and AI tools, and can pick up emerging SEO/GEO capabilities quickly enough to know which product bets are worth making — without needing to personally execute SEO.

Success Metrics

Examples include: booking conversion rate, hotel adoption of DBS, feature adoption, booking-funnel completion, search and AI/GEO visibility for hotels on DBS, customer and hotelier satisfaction, and retention.


Important Clarification

This role is not a traditional Product Owner responsible primarily for backlog management and task assignment. The focus is on owning DBS as a genuinely new product category — one that has to work as a business tool for hotels and as a booking experience travelers actually use.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary plus equity package
  • Define a new product category — DBS sits at the intersection of B2B SaaS, consumer booking, and AI discovery, largely undefined by competitors today
  • Autonomy to experiment, take risks, and drive discovery
  • Work at the intersection of cutting-edge AI and a massive traditional industry

  • Demonstrated track record owning GTM strategy for a subscription, membership, or loyalty program, from positioning through lifecycle, with measurable results.
  • Deep fluency in subscription/loyalty marketing mechanics: you understand member acquisition, onboarding, engagement, and churn, and know how to use marketing to move each lever.
  • A sharp strategic mind that can synthesize consumer research, behavioral data, and competitive signals into positioning and messaging that cuts through
  • Proven ability to influence product roadmaps. You've brought the voice of the customer into planning cycles and shaped what gets built, not just how it gets marketed.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting and defending strategy to VP and C-suite stakeholders.
  • Experience partnering closely with growth, lifecycle/CRM, creative, and data science teams to develop and execute multi-channel campaigns

  • Troubleshoot production issues, perform root-cause analysis, and continuously improve the reliability of data services.
  • Collaborate with data scientists, researchers, analysts, and other engineers to deliver high-quality analytical datasets.

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, data engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Strong experience with PySpark, SQL, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, and Databricks.

  • Experience working with cloud-based data platforms and storage such as AWS S3, Azure Data Lake Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.

  • Understanding of distributed data processing, data modeling, data quality, and pipeline performance optimization.
  • Experience troubleshooting and supporting production data workloads.

  • Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code technologies.
  • Experience with Databricks Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines / Delta Live Tables.
  • Experience implementing data lineage, metadata management, monitoring, and audit-ready logging.
  • Familiarity with Databricks APIs, SDKs, or automation frameworks.

This is a freelance remote role with the flexibility to decide your business hours. Local candidates are preferred but others can still be considered. This role is a great opportunity to supplement your current job or private practice.

We're seeking to partner with International Coaching Federation (ICF) Coaches, Clinical Psychologists, and counsellors to be part of a community working collaboratively to bring greater mental health access to the public to provide mental health coaching.

What You'll Do

  • Support your clients in setting up either person or career goals, relationships, etc
  • Collaboratively work with the internal clinical team by suggesting improvements to the program and the platform.

Requirements

Requirements

  • Has an active International Coaching Federation Certification OR a Master / Postgraduate Diploma training in Counselling
  • Skilled in coaching techniques and/or evidence-based approaches (e.g. Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, DBT, SFBT, etc.)
  • ICF Coaches must have at least 200 coaching hours
  • Counsellors must have at least 300 clinical hours post graduation
  • Candidate must be proficient in English and local language
  • Candidates with prior experience in EAP, counselling working adults or coaching managerial roles are prioritised.

The Consulting Solution Architect - NetApp is a nationally aligned technical pre-sales role within CDW’s National Specialized Presales team. The role focuses on developing comprehensive NetApp solutions and consulting-led engagements for CDW customers across storage, data management, data protection, cyber resiliency, hybrid cloud, and AI-ready infrastructure. The Consulting Solution Architect provides consultative guidance, supports partner product and services sales, scopes service offerings, and fosters strategic relationships that drive business growth.

In this role, the coworker partners with customers, delivery teams, internal sales teams, field Solution Architects, and NetApp to develop and maintain strategic relationships and serve as a trusted advisor. The role provides national technical leadership for complex and strategic opportunities, accelerates pipeline development, enables the field, and helps grow CDW’s NetApp product and services business.

  • Motivated, self-starting, and able to independently perform high-quality work with minimal guidance.

Demonstrate strong understanding of NetApp architecture, products, technologies, and solutions, including ONTAP and related data services, and apply that knowledge to customer-specific recommendations.
  • Team collaboration and leadership: Work effectively with cross-functional sales, services, delivery, partner, and technical teams; lead technical discussions; influence decision-making; and provide guidance, coaching, and mentorship to other coworkers.
  • Customer-focused approach: Demonstrate a customer-centric mindset with strong communication, presentation, discovery, and facilitation skills. Build trusted relationships, understand customer pain points, and explain technical concepts and business value clearly to both technical and executive audiences.
  • Solution design and problem-solving skills: Design and communicate comprehensive solutions that address customer requirements and business challenges. Analyze complex problems, identify appropriate options, build consensus, and resolve technical gaps in proposed solutions.
  • Consulting and commercial skills: Develop assessments, roadmaps, proposals, SOWs, BOMs, and consulting-led recommendations. Connect technical decisions to customer outcomes and support product, software, subscription, and services growth.
  • National engagement: Manage competing priorities across a broad coverage model and collaborate effectively with geographically distributed teams, customers, and partners.
  • Willingness to travel up to 25% or as needed.
  • Current NetApp technical certifications aligned to the role and CDW partner requirements, a plus.
  • Experience architecting NetApp solutions in enterprise, hybrid cloud, virtualization, container, data protection, cyber resiliency, and AI infrastructure environments, a plus.
  • Experience supporting strategic enterprise accounts and complex, multi-practice or multi-million-dollar opportunities, a plus.
  • Consulting or professional services experience, including assessment development and services scoping, a plus.
  • Experience delivering national field enablement, reusable solution assets, partner programs, or go-to-market initiatives, a plus.

jobs.excerpt: About VantageVantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises.
jobs.description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview

This role can be based in Denver, CO following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office, 2 days flexible). Or remote, US.

The Manager, ServiceNow Platform Owner is accountable for day-to-day platform prioritization, roadmap coordination, governance, readiness, supportability, and practical business value tracking for the ServiceNow platform. Reporting to the Platform Director, this role translates platform strategy into practical priorities, coordinates intake and delivery readiness, and ensures stakeholder commitments are visible, sequenced, and supportable.

The role may be consulted on adoption planning and adoption impacts but is not accountable for platform adoption. This position directly manages a ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner and works in close partnership with development, architecture, operations, security, SPM, PMO, finance, procurement, vendors, and business stakeholders; however, it does not directly oversee or manage the development team.

Essential Job Functions

Platform Governance & Standards

  • Define practical standards for ServiceNow intake, prioritization, roadmap management, architecture review, release readiness, documentation, supportability, adoption input, and value tracking.

  • Run ServiceNow governance routines and keep decisions, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and escalations visible and traceable for the Platform Director and stakeholders.

  • Continue maturing ServiceNow governance so it can act as a reusable standard for other enterprise platforms.

  • Ensure ServiceNow functional boards are operational, decision-oriented, and supported by companion product owners who represent functional priorities.

  • Reduce shadow work, unclear ownership, duplicate configuration, unmanaged customization, and unapproved commitments through clear ServiceNow guardrails.

Roadmap, Intake & Prioritization

  • Maintain the ServiceNow roadmap, informed by business priorities, platform strategy, technical considerations, dependencies, risks, releases, and decisions.

  • Ensure work enters through approved intake and is ready enough to sequence responsibly.

  • Own ServiceNow platform content and communications channels, including the SharePoint site/web page, release notes, and bi-weekly platform updates; stakeholder and program updates remain PMO-owned.

  • Manage ServiceNow platform prioritization and coordinate funding assumptions, delivery capacity inputs, architecture decisions, and risk tradeoffs with the Platform Director and partner teams.

Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop the ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner, ensuring clear ownership for technical direction, product priorities, roadmap execution, stakeholder engagement, and platform outcomes.

  • Set expectations for ServiceNow ownership, technical decision discipline, product management, communication, stakeholder management, governance participation, and measurable outcomes.

  • Support hiring, role clarity, performance feedback, development planning, workload balance, and succession planning.

  • Build an accountable ServiceNow team culture that balances speed, quality, platform health, business value, and sustainable operations.

Delivery Readiness & Risk Management

  • Coordinate with development to ensure ServiceNow delivery commitments align to approved decisions, capacity inputs, architecture readiness, release timing, and support readiness.

  • Set minimum readiness expectations for testing, documentation, support handoff, rollback planning, post-release ownership, and adoption-related inputs needed by business or change owners.

  • Escalate risks affecting ServiceNow platform health, stakeholder commitments, budget, staffing, compliance, or enterprise outcomes.

  • Serve as a consulted partner on ServiceNow platform health, technical debt, integration sprawl, customization risk, support complexity, data quality, and value realization where development or execution ownership sits with other teams.

Vendor, Metrics & Escalation Ownership

  • Own large program statements of work with vendors, ensuring scope, deliverables, assumptions, dependencies, handoffs, and acceptance criteria are documented and aligned to ServiceNow platform priorities.

  • Use metrics, usage insights, incident trends, backlog health, vendor performance inputs, and stakeholder feedback to inform prioritization recommendations, SOW adjustments, and resourcing discussions.

  • Set day-to-day ServiceNow governance expectations, require decision traceability, return work that is not ready, manage platform prioritization within agreed guardrails, own large program vendor SOWs, and escalate priorities, risks, funding needs, staffing needs, or exceptions to the Platform Director.

Duties

  • Partner with the Platform Director to translate ServiceNow strategy into an actionable platform roadmap.

  • Coordinate intake, prioritization, governance, and readiness routines across ServiceNow stakeholders.

  • Maintain clear visibility into platform commitments, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and decisions.

  • Partner with architecture, development, security, operations, finance, procurement, PMO, and business stakeholders to sequence work responsibly.

  • Ensure ServiceNow communications, release notes, bi-weekly platform updates, and platform content are clear, current, and aligned to approved decisions.

  • Lead the ServiceNow Architect and ServiceNow Product Owner through clear expectations, coaching, prioritization discipline, and role clarity.

  • Support ServiceNow functional boards and companion product owners in representing business priorities and decision needs.

  • Guide vendor SOW development and alignment to platform priorities, delivery assumptions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

  • Monitor platform health indicators, backlog health, incident trends, stakeholder feedback, and adoption-related inputs to inform prioritization recommendations.

  • Escalate risks, issues, resourcing needs, funding implications, or exceptions that impact ServiceNow platform outcomes.

Job Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in enterprise systems, platform management, ServiceNow, enterprise service management, product management, technology delivery, or program coordination.

  • Experience supporting or managing ServiceNow or enterprise platform operating models, governance routines, roadmaps, intake models, decision tracking, and prioritization processes.

  • Experience leading technical and product-aligned roles, coaching team members, managing performance, and clarifying ownership in a matrixed environment.

  • Strong stakeholder communication skills, with the ability to translate platform, delivery, and risk topics into clear updates, options, and recommendations.

  • Experience working collaboratively with platform directors, architecture, development, security, operations, finance, procurement, PMO, business stakeholders, and vendors without assuming direct ownership of partner teams.

  • Hands-on or leadership experience with ServiceNow modules, platform governance, integrations, automation, reporting, data quality, and release management preferred.

  • Experience in global, infrastructure, operations, data center, construction, or high-growth environments preferred.

  • Experience creating ServiceNow governance forums, role clarity artifacts, decision matrices, staffing plans, dashboards, or executive-ready materials preferred.

  • Ability to manage ServiceNow with practical judgment, an enterprise mindset, and a bias toward clarity and follow-through.

  • Ability to build trust through concise communication, transparent tradeoffs, and consistent follow-through.

  • Ability to coach and hold teams accountable without creating unnecessary process burden.

  • Ability to create a ServiceNow team culture that values ownership, collaboration, responsible escalation, continuous improvement, platform health, and measurable outcomes.

  • Travel requirements: 20% Or could increase as business needs.

Physical Demands and Special Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop or kneel; talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

Additional Details

  • Salary Range: $160,000- $170,000 Base + Bonus (this range is based on Colorado market data and may vary in other locations)

  • This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits.

  • Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including your qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience and may fall outside of the range shown.

We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. We find joy in our work and each other, actively seeking opportunities to inject fun into what we do. Our hard and efficient work is rewarded with an above market total compensation package. We offer a comprehensive suite of health and welfare, retirement, and paid leave benefits exceeding local expectations.

Throughout the year, the advantage of being part of the Vantage team is evident with an array of benefits, recognition, training and development, and the knowledge that your contribution adds value to the company and our community.

jobs.description:
Sr. Accessibility Product Manager

Are you passionate about building accessible products that serve a diverse community of clinicians and healthcare professionals?

Do you thrive in leading complex, cross-functional programs that drive meaningful, measurable impact across a global product portfolio?

About the Role
In this role, you will lead the accessibility program for a broad portfolio of Clinical Solutions products, ensuring they meet evolving accessibility standards and support the needs of a diverse user base. You will set strategy, oversee execution, and guide teams to embed accessibility into product development practices. This position operates with high visibility and contributes directly to product quality, compliance, and customer trust.

Responsibilties

Own the Accessibility Program

  • Assess the current compliance posture, identify gaps, and drive the program from where it is to where it needs to be

  • Own conformance documentation (VPATs/ACRs) across all active products — ensuring everything is current, accurate, and ready for enterprise procurement

  • Partner with Legal on ADA Title III obligations, contractual commitments, and customer inquiries; be the person who knows where the risks are before they become escalations

  • Stay ahead of the legal and regulatory landscape — enforcement trends, emerging state statutes, and international equivalents for our global customer base

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

  • Build and maintain the portfolio-level remediation roadmap across a large suite of products spanning physician, nursing, specialty, and patient engagement categories

  • Work with product managers, engineers, and designers to embed accessibility into how we build — not as an afterthought audit, but as part of discovery, design, and delivery

  • Coordinate a distributed network of accessibility champions embedded in product teams; set direction, maintain standards, and keep execution coherent across teams

  • Own triage for incoming accessibility issues — from customers, audits, and legal — and drive them to resolution

Extend Coverage to Content

  • Accessibility at Elsevier isn't just about the UI layer — clinical content, educational materials, and PDFs all carry their own obligations

  • Work with content authoring teams to ensure alt text, captions, reading order, and PDF accessibility are built into how content is created, not fixed after the fact

Build Visibility and Capability

  • Define the metrics that tell leadership whether the program is working, and report against them consistently

  • Create the standards and guidance that raise baseline accessibility capability across product and engineering teams — reducing reliance on escalation

  • Be the authoritative voice on accessibility for Clinical Solutions; represent the program at the leadership level and in enterprise customer conversations

Requirements

  • 6+ years in product management, with at least 2 years owning a digital accessibility or compliance program at a product-led company

  • Deep working knowledge of WCAG 2.1/2.2, Section 508, and ADA Title III as applied to web and mobile software products

  • Experience producing and defending VPATs / Accessibility Conformance Reports in an enterprise B2B context

  • Proven ability to inherit an existing program, assess its maturity honestly, and drive measurable improvement — you know how to make something significantly better without starting over

  • Experience coordinating distributed ownership models — you've worked across teams where you influence without direct authority

  • Technical fluency sufficient for credible conversations with front-end engineers on ARIA patterns, semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, and screen reader behavior

  • Experience navigating Legal stakeholders and accessibility-related procurement and contractual requirements

Strong Preference

  • Background in health tech, SaaS, or enterprise software with a large, heterogeneous product portfolio

  • Experience with content accessibility — alt text, closed captioning, PDF remediation, authoring tool compliance

  • Hands-on experience with assistive technology testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, ZoomText)

  • Familiarity with automated testing tooling (axe, Lighthouse, Pa11y) and CI/CD integration

  • Exposure to European Accessibility Act / EN 301 549 for international product lines

  • CPACC, WAS, or equivalent IAAP certification

Work in a Way That Works for You
We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.

Working Pattern
Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive.

About the Business
A global leader in information and analytics, we help researchers and healthcare professionals advance science and improve health outcomes for the benefit of society. Building on our publishing heritage, we combine quality information and vast data sets with analytics to support visionary science and research, health education and interactive learning, as well as exceptional healthcare and clinical practice.   • Curiosity and continuous learning
    You stay current on healthcare trends, systems, and procedures to provide thoughtful, informed guidance.

Who Will Thrive in This Role

You will thrive in this role if you are comfortable balancing compassionate member conversations with a fast-paced, high-volume phone environment. The Head of Global Strategic Feasibility and Study Start-Up at BeOne is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the strategic planning and feasibility assessments for global clinical studies. This individual leads the global strategic feasibility team, works with regional strategic feasibility team, and collaborates closely with cross functional stakeholders while leading a team of Study Start Up documentation specialists to accelerate key study level/asset documentation while driving quality and consistency. The Head of Global Strategic Feasibility and Study Start-Up plays a crucial role in shaping the company's global clinical study strategy and decision-making process while directly impacting study-start up timelines. This individual is accountable to establish and improve the global strategic feasibility processes, procedures, and systems and study start-up documentation to strive for continuous optimization.

  • Continuous Improvement: Drive process optimization initiatives to enhance feasibility assessment methodologies, tools, and metrics, ensuring efficiency, quality, and scalability.

Tax Specialist (U.S. Tax Compliance, Preparation & Tax Planning) – Remote | U.S. Hours

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an experienced Tax Specialist to manage U.S. tax preparation, compliance, filings, and tax planning across individual and business entities.

This is a hands-on tax role requiring strong knowledge of U.S. federal and state taxation, IRS requirements, individual and business tax returns, and tax compliance.

You will be responsible for:

  • Preparing and reviewing Forms 1040, 1120, and 1065
  • Managing federal, state, and multi-state tax compliance
  • Handling quarterly estimated taxes and extensions
  • Researching changing tax laws and IRS guidance
  • Responding to tax notices and supporting audits
  • Identifying deductions, credits, and tax-saving opportunities
  • Maintaining accurate, audit-ready tax documentation

If you have strong experience in U.S. tax preparation and compliance and can balance technical accuracy, deadlines, and tax planning, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

U.S. Tax Preparation & Filing

  • Prepare and review individual tax returns (Form 1040)
  • Prepare and review corporate tax returns (Form 1120)
  • Prepare and review partnership returns (Form 1065)
  • Calculate and coordinate quarterly estimated tax payments
  • Prepare and file tax extensions
  • Manage federal and state filing requirements
  • Maintain organized tax calendars and filing schedules
  • Ensure returns are accurate, complete, compliant, and submitted on time

Federal, State & Multi-State Tax Compliance

  • Monitor changes to:
    • IRS guidance
    • Federal tax laws
    • State and local tax requirements
  • Maintain compliance across applicable jurisdictions
  • Support multi-state tax requirements
  • Assist with:
    • Payroll tax
    • Sales tax
    • Property tax
  • Identify potential compliance risks before they result in penalties or missed deadlines
  • Maintain accurate supporting records for tax filings

Tax Planning & Advisory

  • Analyze financial information to identify potential:
    • Tax deductions
    • Credits
    • Tax-saving opportunities
    • Liability reduction strategies
  • Support tax-efficient transaction planning
  • Research tax implications of business and financial decisions
  • Clearly communicate tax considerations and compliance requirements
  • Assist with international tax matters when applicable, including:
    • FBAR
    • FATCA
    • Transfer pricing

IRS Notices, Audits & Tax Inquiries

  • Review and respond to IRS and state tax notices
  • Prepare documentation for audits and regulatory inquiries
  • Maintain organized, audit-ready tax schedules and supporting files
  • Research discrepancies and determine appropriate responses
  • Coordinate with internal teams and external advisors when necessary
  • Track outstanding notices and inquiries through resolution

Tax Research & Documentation

  • Research tax regulations, IRS guidance, and filing requirements
  • Document tax positions and assumptions used in filings
  • Maintain organized supporting schedules and workpapers
  • Keep tax compliance procedures and documentation current
  • Ensure records are complete, accessible, and audit-ready

Accounting & Finance Collaboration

  • Work closely with accounting and finance teams
  • Support month-end and year-end close activities when tax input is required
  • Ensure alignment between financial statements and tax reporting
  • Collaborate with:
    • Finance leadership
    • External CPAs
    • Auditors
    • Tax advisors
  • Resolve discrepancies between accounting records and tax filings

Required Experience & Skills

  • 3+ years of professional U.S. tax preparation, tax compliance, or tax accounting experience
  • Strong understanding of:
    • U.S. federal tax law
    • State tax compliance
    • IRS filing requirements
  • Hands-on experience preparing individual and business tax returns
  • Experience with Forms 1040, 1120, and 1065
  • Experience using professional tax software such as:
    • UltraTax
    • Drake
    • Lacerte
    • ProSeries
    • Similar professional tax platforms
  • Familiarity with IRS e-filing systems and state tax portals
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills
  • Strong reconciliation and analytical abilities
  • Excellent attention to detail and deadline management
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Ability to work independently during U.S. business hours

Nice to Have

  • CPA or Enrolled Agent (EA) certification
  • Master’s degree in Taxation
  • Multi-state tax experience
  • International tax exposure
  • Familiarity with FBAR, FATCA, or transfer pricing
  • Experience supporting:
    • High-net-worth individuals
    • Closely held businesses
    • Multi-entity organizations
  • Industry experience in:
    • SaaS
    • Real estate
    • Professional services
  • Experience handling IRS or state audits and notices
  • Experience working with U.S.-based accounting or tax teams

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You may be especially successful in this role if you:

  • Have strong technical knowledge of U.S. taxation
  • Are highly accurate and detail-oriented
  • Manage filing deadlines without requiring constant oversight
  • Stay current with changing tax laws and regulations
  • Can research complex tax questions independently
  • Proactively identify compliance risks
  • Look for legitimate opportunities to improve tax efficiency
  • Can explain complex tax concepts clearly to non-tax stakeholders
  • Maintain clean, organized, audit-ready documentation

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may include:

  • Reviewing upcoming federal and state filing deadlines
  • Preparing individual, corporate, and partnership tax returns
  • Reviewing tax schedules and reconciliations
  • Calculating estimated tax payments
  • Researching federal or state tax requirements
  • Analyzing financial records for deductions and tax-planning opportunities
  • Responding to IRS or state notices
  • Coordinating with accounting and finance teams
  • Maintaining audit-ready tax documentation
  • Monitoring changes in tax laws and IRS guidance

In short: You ensure tax filings are accurate and timely, compliance risks are controlled, and legitimate tax-planning opportunities are identified.

Key Metrics for Success

  • 100% on-time completion of required tax filings
  • Zero missed filing deadlines
  • Minimal compliance penalties attributable to filing errors
  • Accuracy of tax returns, schedules, and reconciliations
  • Timely resolution of IRS and state notices
  • Strong audit readiness and documentation quality
  • Identification of legitimate tax-saving opportunities
  • Positive feedback from clients, leadership, auditors, and tax stakeholders

Why This Role Stands Out

  • High-impact role across tax, finance, and compliance
  • Hands-on exposure to individual and business taxation
  • Opportunity to work across multiple entities and tax structures
  • Exposure to federal, state, and potentially international tax matters
  • Opportunity to contribute to both tax compliance and planning
  • Direct collaboration with finance leadership and external advisors
  • Fully remote working environment
  • Long-term growth potential within Tax, Accounting, Finance, and Tax Advisory

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  4. Practical Tax Assessment
  5. Client Interview with Finance/Tax Leadership
  6. Offer & Background Verification

Apply Now

If you have strong experience in U.S. tax preparation and compliance, understand federal and state filing requirements, and enjoy combining technical tax work with research and planning, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now to take ownership of tax preparation, compliance, audit support, and tax-planning initiatives in a high-accountability remote environment.

Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin.

JOB OBJECTIVE

The Senior Claims Coverage & General Counselor serves as the Claims organization’s senior legal and technical resource for insurance coverage, claim handling practices, coverage litigation, regulatory matters, extra-contractual exposure, legal process support, and emerging legal issues. The role provides practical guidance across all lines of business to promote timely, consistent, and technically sound claim decisions and outcomes.

Partnering with Claims leadership, Legal, Underwriting, and outside counsel, this position strengthens coverage expertise and claim quality; supports product development and regulatory response; manages significant coverage disputes and related legal expense; and reduces appropriate reliance on outside coverage counsel. The role complements the Legal Department by providing claim-focused coverage, regulatory, and technical expertise within Claims, while coordinating and escalating matters requiring enterprise legal advice, company representation, privilege oversight, or Legal Department ownership.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Provide timely legal and technical guidance on complex commercial and personal lines coverage matters, balancing applicable law, fair claim handling, and business considerations.
  • Analyze policy language, endorsements, exclusions, claim facts, and applicable law; guide coverage investigations; prepare coverage opinions and related legal analyses; and review coverage communications.
  • Advise Claims leadership on dispute-resolution approaches, extra-contractual exposure, bad-faith allegations, claim handling concerns, and other legal risks affecting claim outcomes.
  • Serve as Claims’ senior technical resource for significant coverage litigation and declaratory judgment actions.
  • Partner with Claims leadership, Legal, and outside counsel to develop and execute litigation and resolution strategies, including pleadings, discovery, mediation, settlement, budgets, and trial preparation.
  • Evaluate outside counsel performance and legal expense to improve outcomes, reduce duplication, and manage allocated loss adjustment expense.
  • Guide Claims responses to Department of Insurance complaints, regulatory inquiries, coverage disputes, market conduct examinations, and other regulatory reviews involving Claims operations.
  • Support responses to subpoenas, records and discovery requests, and other legal process involving claim files; coordinate with Legal on matters requiring enterprise advice, company representation, privilege oversight, or Legal Department ownership.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and claim handling requirements, and develop guidance and training to promote compliance and consistent practices.
  • Promote consistent, technically sound coverage positions and claim handling practices across all lines of business.
  • Participate in roundtables addressing complex coverage, exposure evaluation, litigation strategy, reserving, settlement authority, and claim handling issues.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of claim handling best practices, technical standards, coverage guidance, templates, and playbooks.
  • Identify recurring coverage issues, legal and regulatory developments, and claim trends requiring guidance, training, escalation, or operational change.
  • Support quality assurance and file reviews focused on coverage analysis, judgment, documentation, and decision-making, and serve as a trusted advisor to Claims leaders and professionals.
  • Partner with Claims leadership to identify technical development needs and incorporate lessons from coverage matters, litigation, complaints, and regulatory reviews into training.
  • Develop and deliver technical training, coverage resources, and learning tools; mentor claims professionals and leaders to strengthen expertise and judgment in coverage analysis, claim handling, regulatory requirements, extra-contractual risk, and emerging legal issues.
  • Monitor judicial, regulatory, legislative, and industry developments affecting insurance coverage and claim handling, and advise Claims leadership on legal, operational, and risk management implications.
  • Partner with Legal on matters requiring coordination, escalation, enterprise legal guidance, or broader risk management consideration.
  • Partner with Underwriting and Legal to share claim-based insights and emerging loss trends; evaluate proposed policy language, endorsements, and coverage provisions; and recommend appropriate product or policy modifications.
  • Support Claims initiatives involving new tools, processes, or workflows where coverage interpretation, legal risk, regulatory requirements, or claim handling standards are implicated.
  • Handle appropriate coverage opinions, legal research, correspondence, and claim-related consultation internally to reduce reliance on outside coverage counsel.
  • Establish referral criteria for outside coverage counsel and Legal Department involvement, and maintain effective relationships with legal service providers.
  • Evaluate law firm performance, staffing, strategy, budgets, results, and legal spend to improve outcomes, reduce duplication, and manage allocated loss adjustment expense.
  • Partner with Claims leadership and Reinsurance stakeholders on significant losses, coverage issues, treaty interpretation, reporting obligations, recoverability considerations, and matters affecting reinsurer relationships.

OTHER FUNCTIONS

  • Attend mediations, arbitrations, depositions, trials, regulatory meetings, and other proceedings as appropriate.
  • Represent Claims on cross-functional committees, projects, and strategic initiatives.
  • Participate in industry conferences, professional organizations, and continuing legal education activities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school is required.
  • Active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction and in good standing is required.
  • CPCU, AIC, SCLA, or other relevant insurance industry designations are helpful.
  • Minimum of 10 years of experience involving insurance coverage analysis, insurance litigation, claim-related legal support, or comparable property and casualty insurance experience is required.
  • Extensive knowledge of commercial and personal lines insurance coverage, policy interpretation, and claim handling practices is required. Multi-line experience involving commercial auto, general liability, property, workers’ compensation, personal lines, umbrella, professional liability, or specialty coverages is preferred.
  • Experience serving as coverage counsel, claims counsel, claim center general counselor, or in a similar role is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing coverage opinions, reservation of rights letters, denial letters, and other coverage-related communications is required.
  • Strong knowledge of coverage litigation, declaratory judgment actions, extra-contractual and bad-faith exposure, and applicable claim handling requirements is required.
  • Knowledge of insurance regulatory matters, and legal processes including responding to Department of Insurance complaints, market conduct examinations, and subpoenas is required.
  • Experience managing outside counsel, coverage litigation, and legal spending is preferred.
  • Experience supporting underwriting or product teams in policy wording, endorsement development, or product review is preferred.
  • Knowledge of reinsurance principles, reporting obligations, treaty interpretation, and recoverability considerations is preferred.
  • Exceptional legal research, analytical, writing, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to translate complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, practical guidance for claims professionals and business leaders.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions, exercise sound judgment, and build effective partnerships across organizational levels and functions.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex matters, prioritize effectively, and provide timely guidance in a fast-paced claims environment.
  • Ability to handle confidential, sensitive, and potentially privileged matters with appropriate discretion and escalation.
  • Experience developing and delivering technical training for claims professionals and leaders is preferred.

The Medical Director actively uses their medical background, experience, and judgement to make determinations whether requested services, requested level of care, and/or requested site of service should be authorized at the Inpatient level. All work occurs within a context of regulatory compliance, and work is assisted by diverse resources, which may include national clinical guidelines, CMS policies and determinations, clinical reference materials, internal teaching conferences, and other reference sources. Medical Directors will learn Medicare, Medicaid, and Medicare Advantage requirements and will understand how to operationalize this knowledge in their daily work.

The Medical Director’s work includes computer-based review of moderately complex to complex clinical scenarios, review of all submitted clinical records, prioritization of daily work and communication of decisions to internal associates. The clinical scenarios predominantly arise from inpatient or post-acute care environments. A remote possibility exists of doing peer-to-peer discussions with an external provider. Some roles include an overview of coding practices and clinical documentation, dispute/grievance and appeals processes, and outpatient services and equipment, within their scope.

Medical Directors support Humana values, and Humana’s mission, throughout all activities.


Use your skills to make an impact

Responsibilities

The Medical Director provides medical interpretation and determinations whether services provided by other healthcare professionals are in agreement with national guidelines, CMS requirements, Humana policies, clinical standards, and (in some cases) contracts. The ideal candidate supports and collaborates with other team members, other departments, Humana colleagues and the Lead Medical Director. After completion of mentored training, daily work is performed with minimal direction. Enjoys working in a structured environment with expectations for consistency in thinking and authorship. Exercises independence in meeting departmental expectations and meets compliance timelines.

Supports the assigned work with respect to market-wide objectives and community relations as directed.

Required Qualifications

  • MD or DO degree
  • 5+ years of direct clinical patient care experience post residency or fellowship, which preferably includes experience in an inpatient environment and/or related to care of a Medicare type population (disabled or >65 years of age).

  • A current and unrestricted license in at least one jurisdiction and willing to obtain additional license, if required.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Identify and escalate recurring trends or process gaps to leadership to support continuous improvement efforts.

QUALIFICATIONS

Job Description:

At GDIT, people are our differentiator. Our work depends on a Data Analyst joining our team to support Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services anti-fraud activities.

As a Data Analyst supporting the Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership (HFPP), you will develop fraud, waste and abuse (FWA) analytics from concept to finished product at the Trusted Third Party (TTP), working against a multi-billion record claims warehouse assembled from dozens of public and private healthcare payers. HFPP Partners and the client bring the questions. You turn them into analytics that identify aberrant billing and hold up to scrutiny. You will engage with healthcare claims and FWA analytics working alongside experienced Subject Matter Experts, and you do need to be genuinely strong with data.

***Work visa sponsorship will not be provided for this position. This is a remote role. Candidates must reside in the United States.

HOW A HEALTHCARE CLAIMS DATA ANALYST WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

  • Working with a multi-disciplinary team of Data Scientists, Business Intelligence Developers and FWA Subject Matter Experts. Our team is 100% remote and distributed throughout the country.

  • Translating Partner and client requests into specifiable analytic questions, including determining what can and cannot be answered with the data available and raising that early rather than late.

  • Developing FWA analytics end to end, building the analytic logic in SQL and Python against billions of claim records, testing it, and refining it in collaboration with FWA Subject Matter Experts until it identifies something real.

  • Separating genuine aberrancy from patterns fully explained by legitimate clinical practice, coverage policy or claim edits, recognizing that the mundane explanation is usually the correct one and that finding it before a Partner does is part of the work.

  • Documenting methodology, assumptions and data lineage so that each analytic can be reproduced and incorporated into the TTP analytic suite by another team without the original analyst present.

  • Documenting findings and present results to internal stakeholders, and will participate in Partner discussions to clarify analytic requirements.

  • Managing several concurrent requests against firm deadlines within a queue driven by Partner and client demand.

jobs.excerpt: ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.
jobs.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.

While the vast majority of ProPublica’s work comes from our staff, we occasionally consider supporting ambitious accountability stories or projects from independent journalists whose ideas align with the mission of our organization.

Here’s what journalists submitting proposals should know.

We’re open to investigations that are revelatory or substantially advance what is known on a subject of importance. The investigation should have the potential to trigger needed reforms by identifying a problem, who’s responsible and what should change. It should also clearly show harm. The investigation can be rooted in a place or focus on a person, but it should illuminate an issue of broader relevance.

The best proposals have a clear hypothesis, typically based on significant reporting: They don’t wonder whether something bad is happening, they know it. Please include not only a general description of the topic, but also a sense of the anecdotes/data/documents you have gathered, what you expect to find and possible accountability stories you want to tell.

In addition, applicants should detail, as much as is possible at the outset, what an investigation will require: data work, travel, obtaining public records. It’s also important for us to know what data, documents and/or source relationships the reporter already has. Finally, we’d like to hear a bit about why you are particularly suited to do this investigation.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission. Questions? Send an email to . No phone calls, please.

For those proposals we accept, we pay competitive freelance rates, including reporting expenses. Freelancers are independent contractors and will not be treated by ProPublica as employees for any purpose.

Independent contractors are responsible for paying any required taxes on any compensation received and for understanding the applicable tax laws. We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission.

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

We are dedicated to improving our newsroom, in part by better reflecting the people we cover. (Here is a breakdown of our staff.) We are committed to diversity and building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and ages. And we are taking steps to meet that commitment. We especially encourage members of traditionally underrepresented communities to apply, including women, people of color, LGBTQ+ people and people with disabilities. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Subscription Management - SER
jobs.excerpt: Our world is transforming, and PTC is leading the way.
jobs.description:
Our world is transforming, and PTC is leading the way. Our software brings the physical and digital worlds together, enabling companies to improve operations, create better products, and empower people in all aspects of their business.

Our people make all the difference in our success. Today, we are a global team of nearly 7,000 and our main objective is to create opportunities for our team members to explore, learn, and grow – all while seeing their ideas come to life and celebrating the differences that make us who we are and the work we do possible.

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced commercial leader to lead the Southern Europe Region (SER) Subscription Management team. This role is responsible for driving subscription renewal performance, ARR retention, churn mitigation, forecasting accuracy, commercial lifecycle management, and strategic business programs across both direct and channel business.

The successful candidate will lead a regional team of Subscription Managers while partnering closely with Sales, Customer Success, Channel organizations, Operations, Legal, Finance, and Product Management. The role combines people leadership, commercial strategy, operational excellence, and transformation leadership to maximize customer retention and recurring revenue growth.

A core expectation is the ability to convert strategy into adopted change. The candidate must demonstrate, with concrete examples, how they align stakeholders with competing priorities, create clarity on the business case for change, secure commitment, remove resistance, and drive adoption through disciplined execution, communication, and measurable follow-through.

Equally critical is a hands-on coaching orientation. The candidate must prove that they can set explicit performance expectations, observe real work, give timely and direct feedback, coach renewal strategy and stakeholder engagement, build individual development plans, and follow through until behavior and business outcomes improve.

The position plays a critical role in leading key business motions including renewal governance, contract optimization and modernization, forecast management, partner enablement, and cross-functional transformation programs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own renewal performance, customer retention, ARR preservation, churn mitigation, forecast accuracy, and commercial lifecycle execution for SER across direct and channel business.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing regional Subscription Management team with clear priorities, strong accountability, transparency, customer focus, continuous learning, and a One Team mindset.
  • Drive strategic initiatives and commercial transformation programs by building the stakeholder map, aligning Sales, Customer Success, Channel, Finance, Legal, Operations, and Product around the business case, anticipating friction, and creating a practical adoption plan.
  • Establish a clear operating rhythm for cross-functional alignment, escalation, decision-making, communication, and adoption tracking, ensuring that agreed changes move from discussion to executed behavior.
  • Provide leadership and guidance on complex renewals, customer negotiations, commercial escalations, contract modernization, and partner-led business opportunities.
  • Coach Subscription Managers through specific behaviors: qualification of renewal risks, executive-level account planning, commercial negotiation preparation, stakeholder mapping, forecast hygiene, customer value articulation, and post-renewal learning reviews.
  • Set measurable expectations, inspect work through forecast reviews and deal coaching, provide direct feedback, document development actions, and hold team members accountable for improvement.
  • Use data, governance adherence, process discipline, and clear business reviews to identify risks and opportunities early and improve predictability and scalable execution.
  • Build strong relationships with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders to maximize business outcomes and reinforce Subscription Management as a trusted commercial partner.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate builds a highly engaged, collaborative, and accountable team that consistently delivers strong renewal performance while maintaining a positive and supportive culture.

They are recognized as a leader who can make change happen, not only talk about it. Stakeholders understand the why, know what is expected of them, commit to the new way of working, and see progress through clear communication, governance, adoption tracking, and measurable behavior change.

Their coaching has visible impact. Team members improve how they prepare renewals, manage risk, engage stakeholders, articulate customer value, inspect forecasts, and learn from outcomes. Coaching is not generic encouragement; it is specific, observable, repeated, and connected to measurable business behaviors, with clear feedback and follow-up.

Success is demonstrated through strong business outcomes, effective cross-functional partnerships, operational excellence, talent development, and a culture where communication, knowledge sharing, innovation, and continuous improvement are embedded in the way the team operates.

Required Qualifications

Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in subscription management, renewals, customer success, sales operations, commercial operations, or related fields.
  • 3+ years of people leadership experience with clear evidence of developing talent and raising performance standards.
  • Proven experience managing complex recurring revenue businesses.
  • Experience working with indirect/channel sales models.
  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional initiatives and business transformation programs where stakeholder adoption was required, including evidence of stakeholder mapping, resistance management, communication rhythm, adoption metrics, and measurable behavior or outcome change.
  • Demonstrated experience coaching commercial teams through concrete deal, forecast, negotiation, risk, and stakeholder-management scenarios, including diagnosis of performance gaps, specific interventions, direct feedback, follow-up, and measured improvement.

Skills & Competencies

  • Executive-level communication and stakeholder management with the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and geographies.
  • Change leadership: can diagnose resistance, build coalitions, create adoption plans, communicate the why, hold stakeholders accountable for execution, and show how change moved from alignment to adopted behavior.
  • Commercial acumen and strong business judgment.
  • Forecasting and analytical capability with the discipline to translate insights into action.
  • Strategic thinking with strong operational execution.
  • Prescriptive coaching capability: can observe performance, identify the specific gap, give direct feedback, define the expected behavior, follow up until improvement is visible, and connect coaching to renewal, forecast, negotiation, or stakeholder-management outcomes.
  • Ability to influence without authority while remaining clear, constructive, and outcome-oriented.
  • Customer-centric mindset with a focus on business outcomes.

Preferred Background

  • Experience in enterprise software, SaaS, PLM, CAD, or technology industries.
  • Experience managing international teams and complex regional businesses.
  • Familiarity with CRM and forecasting systems such as Salesforce.
  • Experience supporting large channel ecosystems and partner-led business models.

Life at PTC is about more than working with today’s most cutting-edge technologies to transform the physical world. It’s about showing up as you are and working alongside some of today’s most talented industry leaders to transform the world around you.

If you share our passion for problem-solving through innovation, you’ll likely become just as passionate about the PTC experience as we are. Are you ready to explore your next career move with us?

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

We are seeking a Salesforce Administrator to support, maintain, and enhance the Salesforce platform as business needs evolve. This role will partner with business stakeholders to improve processes, configure practical solutions, support users, maintain data quality, and help ensure the platform operates efficiently and securely. The ideal candidate is an administrator early in their Salesforce career with 1–3 years of Salesforce Administration experience, holds multiple Salesforce certifications, and brings curiosity, accountability, and a strong desire to continue learning and growing within the Salesforce ecosystem.

Salesforce Administration, Configuration & System Maintenance

  • Administer and maintain the Salesforce platform, including user setup, profiles, permission sets, roles, sharing rules, and security settings.

  • Ensure Salesforce configurations align with established governance, security, scalability, and platform best practices.

User Support, Training & Documentation

  • Serve as the team’s initial point of contact for Salesforce user questions, support requests, and enhancement ideas.
  • Provide end-user support and troubleshooting to improve system adoption, productivity, and user experience.
  • Develop, maintain, and update user guides, training materials, knowledge articles, release notes, and support documentation.
  • Support onboarding and training of new users and provide guidance regarding Salesforce capabilities and best practices.

Reporting, Analytics & Data Quality

  • Create and maintain reports, dashboards, and analytics that provide actionable insights for business stakeholders.
  • Perform regular data quality reviews, audits, validation checks, deduplication efforts, and other activities to ensure data integrity and accuracy.
  • Support data imports, exports, mass updates, and data maintenance activities using approved tools and processes.
  • Partner with stakeholders to define reporting requirements and deliver meaningful business metrics and operational insights.

Business Process Improvement & Automation

  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand business processes, gather requirements, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Translate business needs into Salesforce configuration changes, workflow enhancements, and declarative automation solutions.
  • Identify recurring issues, inefficiencies, or manual processes and recommend solutions that improve operational effectiveness and user experience.

Testing, Release Management & Governance

  • Participate in testing, quality assurance, user acceptance testing (UAT), and validation of new functionality, enhancements, and system changes.
  • Support change management and release management processes by documenting, testing, and deploying configuration changes.
  • Maintain system, process, configuration, and support documentation to ensure knowledge sharing and operational continuity.
  • Support security reviews, audits, compliance initiatives, and governance activities as required.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Lead System Administrator, Solutions Engineers, Developers, project managers, and business stakeholders to support Salesforce enhancements and ensure solutions meet business needs.
  • Stay current on Salesforce releases, new features, certifications, and industry best practices, and recommend platform improvements when appropriate.
  • Contribute to the ongoing optimization of the Salesforce platform by identifying opportunities to improve performance, usability, security, and scalability.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Business, or a related field and 1-3 years hands-on experience supporting business users as a Salesforce Administrator, with strong knowledge of Sales Cloud, Service Cloud with Omni-Channel, Lightning Experience, Flows, and complex reporting and dashboards; familiarity with LWCs, Apex, SOQL, and triggers preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Salesforce Administrator certification required; additional certifications strongly preferred.

DESIRED ATTRIBUTES

  • Familiarity with CI/CD tools, release pipelines, and source control best practices (i.e. Azure DevOps, Gearset, Git).
  • Experience troubleshooting user issues and managing data quality initiatives.
  • Experience with strict security models and access management.
  • Experience working in Agile environments.
  • Demonstrated ownership of assigned work with strong follow-through and accountability.
  • Experience with healthcare or growth-focused organizations.
  • Strong customer service mindset and commitment to user success.
  • Strong problem solving and analytical thinking skills, focused on root-cause analysis.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build relationships across technical and business teams.
  • Highly organized and meticulous; excels at managing numerous priorities concurrently with strong attention to detail and commitment to delivery quality.
  • Able to work independently in dynamic, fast-paced environments.
  • Eager to learn new Salesforce capabilities and continuously develop technical expertise.
  • Ability to balance operational support with long-term platform improvements.
  • Leverages AI tools to innovate, augment productivity, improve solution quality, and accelerate delivery across analysis, configuration, testing, and documentation.

Pay Range: $75,000 - $90,000/yr
